transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I'm here because I've been having a really hard time staying in my seat lately. I constantly feel the urge to get up and walk around, even during meetings or times when I'm expected to sit still.
Do you also have trouble focusing on tasks, following through on instructions, or often make careless mistakes at work or in daily activities?
No, I don't really have trouble focusing on tasks or following instructions, and I don't make many careless mistakes. My main issue is just the physical restlessness and constantly needing to get up.
Do you often feel the need to interrupt others when they're talking or have trouble waiting your turn in conversations or activities?
No, I don't think I really struggle with that. Interrupting others or waiting my turn hasn't really been an issue for me.

{
  "category": "duration",
  "subcategory": "symptom duration",
  "question": "Have these symptoms of restlessness been present since childhood, or did they start more recently?"

I've noticed them being much more of a problem over the last seven months, but they actually first started back in my childhood. I can remember struggling with staying in my seat even before I was 12 years old.
Are these symptoms causing significant difficulty in your daily life, such as at work, in relationships, or in other important areas of functioning?
To be honest, I'm not really sure how much it impacts my work or relationships. I haven't given much thought to how it affects those areas of my life.

{
  "category": "functional assessment",
  "subcategory": "occupational impact",
  "question": "Have you received any feedback at work about your restlessness, such as from supervisors or colleagues, or do you find it hard to stay seated during important meetings?"

Yes, I find it incredibly difficult to stay seated during long meetings, and I often end up getting up or leaving my seat entirely. My colleagues have definitely noticed me pacing around, though I haven't gotten any official feedback from my boss yet.

{
  "category": "symptom presence",
  "subcategory": "hyperactivity",
  "question": "Do you also experience feelings of inner restlessness or an inability to relax, even when you're not moving around?"

No, I don't really feel an inner restlessness or a constant inability to relax when I'm sitting still. For me, it's more just a physical urge to get up and move, rather than feeling tense or restless on the inside.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "medical history",
  "question": "Have you ever been evaluated for or diagnosed with any neurological conditions, such as restless legs syndrome or another movement disorder?"
No, I've never been diagnosed with or evaluated for any neurological conditions, including restless legs syndrome. I don't have any history of movement disorders either.
Does the urge to move improve when you're able to walk around, or does it persist even after you've gotten up and moved?
I'm not really sure and I haven't thought about it in that way. I just know that I feel a very strong need to get up and walk around whenever I'm expected to stay seated.

{
  "category": "symptom response",
  "subcategory": "relief with activity",
  "question": "When you do get up and walk around, does the urge to move go away, or does it keep coming back immediately?"
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't paid close attention to whether the urge goes away or comes back immediately after I walk around.
